author: Cognexa team
title: What should AI be allowed to speed up?
lede: Speed needs direction. Start with the decision.
intro: Most teams ask what AI can do. A more useful question is which decisions are safe to hand over, which need a check, and which should stay with a person. The answer depends on the cost of a wrong call.

s.heading: Sort work by the cost of being wrong
s.text: Drafting a summary and approving a refund are very different tasks. We map each task by how reversible its outcome is and how much judgement it needs. Low-risk, reversible work is where speed pays first.

s.heading: Add a review where judgement matters
s.text: Some work can be sped up and then checked. The check should be designed in advance: who looks, what they look for, and what they can change. Without it, people either trust the output too much or redo it from scratch.

s.heading: Keep some decisions human
s.text: Choices that affect trust, safety or fairness deserve a named person. AI can prepare the evidence. The call stays with someone who can explain it to the customer.

quote: Speed is a gain only when someone still owns the decision.

call.text: What happens if this output is wrong?
Who reviews it, and how quickly?
What does the reviewer lose by skipping the check?
